title: Firing the decision sweep
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state Turing machine with Boolean symbols, let $x,y$ be Boolean words, let $bits$ be a Boolean selector encoding, let $P$ be a valid input-head position for $y$, and let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on $x$. Given auxiliary tape contents $\tau_C,\tau_O$, positions $z_C,z_O$, an optional state $oq$, an output register $r$, and a Boolean tag $b$ that correctly marks the boundary position of $c$'s input head, if $\tau_O(z_O)$ contains true, then there is a tag $b'$ correctly marking the boundary position after one decoded-selector walk step on $c$ such that one step of the constructed machine gives the waiting-return configuration with that walked configuration, with $\tau_O(z_O)$ changed to false and the auxiliary head moved to $z_O-1$.
